title: edge-network-delegation-contract-ux-sketch
content:
Purpose and context:

This note sketches a lightweight UX + contract for customer-managed network changes that require Redwood operator review or delegated approval. The goal is a minimal, auditable exchange that: 
- lets customers retain control of their edge/networking stack,
- enables optional operator participation for rapid remediation or policy attestations,
- produces compact audit evidence and acceptance tokens suitable for retention and later forensic queries.

Why this is different from earlier PRDs: many drafts focus on full attestation bundles (large evidence blobs). We want an option that is intentionally small (for low-bandwidth customers) and ergonomically simple for operators to act on while preserving strong proofs for audits.

Key user journeys (sketch):

1) Customer-initiated VPC change requiring approval
- Customer engineer opens the Redwood Private console -> "Network changes" -> submit change package.
- Package includes: short rationale (text), patch diff (optional small), planned window, rollback plan (free text), and a lightweight network snapshot hash (see telemetry).
- Submit triggers local validation (lint rules), then queued for approval.
- UX: show 'required approvals' badge (none | operator | delegated-team).

2) Delegated approval (preferred for customers who want faster operations)
- Customer configures a delegation contract: maps a customer role (e.g., "netops") to an operator capability with constraints (time windows, max scope, emergency-only flag).
- When a change matches the contract, the delegated approver (an operator ID or vendor ID) can approve without full manual review.
- Approver action results in an approval token (signed, minimal JSON) returned to the customer as proof-of-approval.

3) Operator-assisted approval (escalation path)
- If lint or heuristics flag risk, Redwood operator receives alert in Console + optional Slack/Email.
- Operator can: approve, request more info, or reject. Each decision emits a signed event and links to the change snapshot.

Contract primitives (data model - intentionally small):
- change_id: opaque UUID string
- actor: principal (email or service-id)
- change_summary: short text (<= 512 chars)
- scope_tags: list of short tags (e.g., ingress, egress, nat)
- snapshot_hash: base64url(sha256 of minimal snapshot)
- requested_window: iso8601 window (start/end)
- requested_rollforward_ok: boolean (if false, operator must explicitly approve rollforward)
- approval_policy_id: short id
- approval_token: present only after approval (signed compact token, see below)

Approval token (compact evidence artifact):
- format: JWT-like compact JSON with fields: change_id, approver_id, approval_ts, policy_digest, sig
- size target: < 2kb when base64 encoded
- stored in audit index for quick retrieval; raw change payloads can be optional (retention policy decides)

Telemetry and audit events (minimal set):
- event: change.submitted {change_id, actor, policy}
- event: change.validated {change_id, ok|flags}
- event: change.escalated {change_id, reason}
- event: approval.issued {change_id, approver_id, token_id}
- event: approval.rejected {change_id, approver_id, reason}
- event: change.executed {change_id, executor_id, outcome}
Each event must record a snapshot_hash and be indexed by customer_id, change_id, and time.

Retention and privacy tradeoffs:
- Default retention: approval tokens and events retained 7 years (enterprise default).
- Raw diffs and full snapshots: opt-in retention (customers can choose to persist full evidence to Redwood S3 or export to their own storage).
- Minimal mode: keep only event traces + snapshot_hash (small footprint).

UX mock flows (high level):
- Submit -> Inline lint/preview -> Request approval -> Show who can approve (delegated / operator) -> Fast-approve (if delegation) -> Receipt + token in console -> Optional webhooks to customer ops.

Edge cases and questions (open):
- How granular should delegation contracts be? Per-namespace, per-tag, or global? Proposal: start per-namespace + scope_tags.
- Emergency overrides: allow 1-click emergency approval by operator with later audit justification. Should we require a second operator attestation for high-severity operations?
- Signing keys: operators will use Redwood-managed keys; customers should be able to verify signatures against a published Redwood cert bundle. For delegated vendor operators, we need a cross-signed cert model.
- Offline approvals: support pre-signed offline tokens that customers can present during maintenance windows? Security risk: tokens could be stolen; if implemented, must support one-time-use nonce and short TTL (<= 15m).

Acceptance criteria for an MVP (alpha):
- Customers can submit a change with minimal metadata and receive events in the console.
- Delegation contracts can be created and matched against changes.
- When matched, delegated approver can approve via console or API; an approval token is generated and verifiable.
- Events and approval tokens are searchable by change_id and customer_id in Console (7-day retention in alpha).
- Basic lint rules block trivial misconfigurations and surface soft warnings to approvers.

Non-goals for alpha:
- Full forensic evidence export UI.
- Long-term archival automation (beyond allowing manual export).
- Complex multi-approver orchestration (beyond simple delegated vs operator).

Implementation notes / infra considerations:
- Compact snapshot: only capture critical fields (route table hashes, firewall ruleset metadata, certificate fingerprints). No raw secrets.
- Use existing audit pipeline (observability team) to index events; add compact token storage to the approved evidence index.
- Signing: leverage HSM-backed key in KMS; store public certs in a published bundle for verification.
- UI: small "approval drawer" component; API: /changes/{id}/approve -> returns token; /changes/{id}/events -> returns indexed events.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Sync with Security on signing model (owner: Sofia Patel) – 2025-01-20
- Draft API contract and sample token verifier in SDKs (owner: Miguel Ramirez) – 2025-01-27
- UX quick prototype for console drawer (owner: Aisha Carter) – 2025-02-05
- Create test harness for delegation matching rules (owner: Ethan Zhou) – 2025-02-10

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "proof-of-execution" follow-up token issued by the executor after the change that references the approval token (chaining evidence).
- When exporting to customer S3, include a lightweight index file mapping change_id -> token_id -> snapshot_hash for quick reconciliation.
- Explore optional PKI model so customers can trust operator signatures without contacting Redwood (useful for air-gapped customers).

Short scenarios to keep in mind while designing:
- Large enterprise with internal netops delegates daily low-risk firewall tweaks to Redwood operators during business hours.
- Regulated customer wants every VPC change approved by their own SOC; they will opt-out of delegation and require operator escalation only for emergency rollback.
- Remote site (low bandwidth) wants only tokens + event traces to be stored with full payloads exported to customer-owned storage during weekly sync windows.

If this approach looks reasonable, I'll iterate into a one-page API / token spec and a small console mock to demo at the next product sync.

End of sketch.
summary: Lightweight UX and compact approval token contract for delegated and operator-mediated customer network changes, focused on minimal evidence artifacts and practical retention tradeoffs.
